title: Admin Bridge: Task-runner with Safety Layers and Dry-Run Sandbox
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create 'Admin Bridge', a compact task-runner service that turns curated runbook flows into auditable, idempotent tasks. Features: REST + CLI entrypoints, dry-run simulation, MFA-backed confirmations for high-risk steps, temporary JIT impersonation credentials, encrypted input blobs, and Console trace integration. Replace ad-hoc SSH/scripts for administrative actions and ensure every execution is observable and reviewable.
acceptance_criteria: REST API and CLI can submit and list task runs and return step-level status
Dry-run mode produces a step-by-step planned actions diff with no side effects
High-risk steps require an explicit MFA confirmation within the UI or CLI before execute
Execution metadata (request ID, user, template version, inputs redacted) is recorded to Audit Log and visible in Console traces
JIT role impersonation issues ephemeral creds that expire and are scoped to the run
Secrets are redacted in logs and validated by security tests
Sandbox E2E harness can run canonical runbook examples without touching prod resources
Per-step telemetry emitted: latency_ms, success, error_code, and estimated cost_tokens
tasks: Define task schema: step types, preconditions, outputs, rollback hints
Design REST API and CLI UX for submission, dry-run, approve, and cancel
Implement dry-run executor that validates preconditions and simulates side effects
Build MFA confirmation flow (web + CLI) and integrate with existing SSO/JIT policies
Add JIT role impersonation connector for AWS/GCP and rotate ephemeral creds
Hook executions to Console tracing and Audit Log with redaction middleware
Create E2E sandbox cluster and test harness for safe real-runbook validation
Author safety guidance, templates for common admin tasks, and developer docs
Run security review, threat model, and automated redaction tests
decisions: Adopt explicit task-graph model (ordered steps) rather than executing arbitrary shell scripts to enable tracing and partial replays
Persist only redacted inputs in plain audit logs; store full inputs encrypted with KMS and require ticketed access for retrieval
Dry-run will run validations and compute diffs but not call mutating APIs; a separate 'apply' action performs mutations
Interactive confirmations are required for steps labelled 'high-risk' by policy; this includes schema migrations and user access grants
